extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of literature (undergraduate/graduate survey courses); readers preparing author studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding questions and reading-suggestion criteria for studying and evaluating individual authors' works (style, themes, originality, influence, and place in literature). Intended to direct student analyses and classroom reports on specific authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative importance of setting and atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the relative importance of these to plot and character? Is the author's main interest in developing a story, in creating characters that live, or in suggesting particular phases of life, each with its own physical and emotional atmosphere?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how setting/atmosphere function in relation to plot and character — do they drive action, reveal character, or chiefly evoke phases of life?

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidences of originality
rubrics_metrics.description: What evidences of originality do you find in his books?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for distinctive themes, techniques, treatments, or perspectives that set the author apart from contemporaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realist vs. romanticist stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the author a realist or a romanticist? Is it true, as has been said, that he stands midway between the 'unrelieved realism' of the new school of writers and the 'genteel moralism' of the old?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position the author on the realism–romanticism spectrum using examples from texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to specific critical charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider these two criticisms of Mr. Hergesheimer's work: (1) He aims to set down 'relative truth ... the colors and scents and emotions of existence'; and (2) he is at times as much concerned 'with the stuffs as with the stuff of life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh textual evidence for and against these characterizations; analyze whether focus on sensory detail is an asset or defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of style: suggestion, diction, rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a special study of his style: (1) of his use of suggestion; (2) of his choice of words; (3) of his feeling for rhythm. It is true that there is both art and artifice in his methods?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze examples for suggestive technique, word choice and cadence; assess balance between art and artifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to national literature and prognosis
rubrics_metrics.description: In what ways, if any, has he made actual contribution to American literature? Can you prophesy as to his future?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess concrete contributions (themes, innovations, influence) and argue for likely enduring reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social criticism vs character-focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of Mr. Herrick's work must be regarded as primarily social criticism of American life. Does the interest tend to centre rather upon the problems of the characters, growing out of their circumstances, or upon the characters themselves?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether novels prioritize sociological issues or psychological/individual development; use passages demonstrating emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and breadth versus intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is Mr. Herrick's work more notable for scope and breadth or for intensity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare works for panoramic range versus concentrated intensity; cite structural and tonal evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic qualities in prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Note, especially in the novels previous to 1905, the conscientious artistry, the compactness of structure, and the unity of tone commonly associated with poetry. What other qualities characteristic of poetry appear in Mr. Herrick's work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify poetic devices (imagery, compression, rhythm, tonal unity) present in prose and evaluate their effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative study of structure across works
rubrics_metrics.description: With the structure of his earlier work compare that of the Memoirs of an American Citizen as showing an attempt at greater breadth of canvas and greater variety of tone. Trace this attempt further in his later work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map structural shifts across career: form, scope, variety of tone; discuss whether shifts succeed artistically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of a theory of the novelist's art
rubrics_metrics.description: What evidences do you find in Mr. Herrick's novels of a carefully wrought theory of the art of the novelist?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate explicit or implicit statements of craft (plot, character, narration) within texts and paratexts; infer the author's theoretical commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical/psychological judgment ('discouraged idealist')
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone has called Mr. Herrick 'a discouraged idealist.' Is this just?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess biographical and textual evidence to support or refute such psychological characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with life and theory for appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: For just appraisement of Mr. Howells, it is necessary to be familiar with the facts of his life, and with his theories of fiction. For his life the two autobiographical books Years of My Youth and My Literary Passions are most valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use autobiographical sources and Howells's own critical writings to contextualize and judge his fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping books by source material
rubrics_metrics.description: Group the books of Howells according to the sources of the material: (1) those growing out of his early life in Ohio; (2) those growing out of his life abroad; (3) those growing out of his life in Boston and New York. Subdivide further by influence (e.g., before/after Tolstoi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify works by provenance and trace thematic/tonal differences tied to those sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of sociological interest on artistic value
rubrics_metrics.description: Does Mr. Howells's interest in sociological problems add to or lessen the final value of his work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether sociological themes enrich or detract from literary quality; support with textual analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of the 'panoramic theory' (coherence and 'rounding off')
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Van Wyck Brooks's remark on Howells's 'panoramic theory' as a test: 'To make a work of art, it is necessary to take a piece out of life and round it off...' Consider whether works are 'perfectly rounded off' and characters proportioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 'rounded off piece of life' standard to Howells's works; judge unity and proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of stylistic elements (clarity, compression, exactness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Howells's style: clearness, compression, verbal exactness and unforced and seemingly unconscious felicity of phrasing — try to analyze it into its elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break down sentences for length, diction, syntax and phrasing to show where these qualities arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment of future literary reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you make any judgment now as to Howells's future place in American literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh influences, innovations, and reception to predict lasting significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin study with author's prefaces and critical essays
rubrics_metrics.description: A good approach to the work of Henry James is through the three articles from the Quarterly Review and the prefaces to his definitive edition; study prefaces for theory of the novel and method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the author's own theoretical statements (prefaces, essays) as keys to interpreting fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to authorial method: 'overtreating' and building detail
rubrics_metrics.description: James's tendency to 'overtreat' (pile brick upon brick) rather than undertreat; attention to effect of detail and the process by which he constructs interest from characters and minute touches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze degree of elaboration/detail and its relation to narrative effect; consider criticisms of 'thinness' vs richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preoccupation with 'the art of life' (subject and morality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember the clue: 'His one preoccupation was the criticism, for his own purpose, of the art of life.' The quality and capacity of the artist's 'prime sensibility' is central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret works in light of James's moral/aesthetic preoccupations and how they shape subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of author's limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider suggestions of Mr. James's limitations (e.g., tone-deafness, lack of verse, failures as a dramatist) and how they affect his output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor non-literary limitations or failed experiments into evaluation of the oeuvre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place in sequence of European novelists
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess James's place as follower of Balzac, Flaubert, De Maupassant, and Turgenev and as predecessor of Conrad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare techniques, themes, and influence across national and chronological lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate judgment before and after method change
rubrics_metrics.description: Early in the nineties a great change in method came about in James's work; judge separately typical books written before this change and others written after; read several books of the period of change and decide what happened and whether or not it enhanced the value of his work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform periodized comparisons to evaluate impact of stylistic/methodological shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze stylistic influence on critics
rubrics_metrics.description: One remarkable fact is James's style's influence upon the critics who write about him. A close analysis of its qualities—sentence length, the order and placing of the parts of the sentence, punctuation, vocabulary, etc., might bring a more definite understanding of the reasons for this influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study technical sentence-level features and track how they shaped critical discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare family members' works (Henry vs William James)
rubrics_metrics.description: A comparison of the work and qualities of Henry and William James might be made a valuable contribution to criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast literary and philosophical aims, styles, and themes across siblings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study cultural affinity and national attitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: For a student familiar with Europe, study the reasons for James's affinity with Europe and dislike for American life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate biographical, cultural, and textual evidence for transatlantic orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments for permanence in literature
rubrics_metrics.description: What different types of reasons can you bring to show that Henry James is likely to be a permanent force in American literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble formal, thematic, historical, and influence-based arguments for enduring significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin criticism with author's autobiography to understand perspective (Huneker)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an understanding of Mr. Huneker's criticisms, it is well to begin with his autobiography (Steeplejack).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use autobiographical material to situate critical positions and critical voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge poet by a chosen period
rubrics_metrics.description: Kilmer wished to be judged by poetry written after October, 1913, and to discard all earlier work. Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider phases in a poet's career and justify choice of a canonical period for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace influences on a poet's work
rubrics_metrics.description: The following influences are traceable in his poetry: (1) Francis Thompson, Coventry Patmore, and earlier Catholic poets; (2) his mother's musical talent; (3) his journalistic work; (4) the War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and discuss how listed biographical/cultural influences manifest in poetic language and themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use letters to illustrate poetic qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Kilmer's letters illustrate and explain the qualities of his work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on correspondence as documentary evidence of intent, influences, and aesthetic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect the unexpected in rebellious modern poets (Kreymborg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Kreymborg is a rebel against all conventions of form and content in poetry. Consequently, the one thing to be expected in his work is the unexpected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach texts anticipating formal and thematic experimentation; evaluate sincerity and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge sincerity versus posing
rubrics_metrics.description: How far his utterances are sincere and how far posed, each reader must judge for himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genuine expressive moments from affectation by examining recurring patterns and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remember contemporary art movements when reading
rubrics_metrics.description: The new movements in art—Futurist, Cubist, Vorticist—should be remembered in studying Mr. Kreymborg's verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize poetry within concurrent visual/avant-garde movements to explain formal choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess economy in words
rubrics_metrics.description: What is to be said of his economy in words?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze concision, redundancy, and verbal economy in poems and their aesthetic implications.
